  "text": "The key scraped in the lock. Mara’s father braced his shoulder against the stone door, but it did not move. The harbor master pointed to the catch. Its iron tongue held fast.

“Who shut it?” the voice asked again.

Mara bent toward the pipe. “Who are you?”

A pause. Then: “The keeper. Open the gate before the pressure breaks the quay.”

The harbor master seized the lantern and held it over the brass plate. Beneath the scratched-out instructions, a narrow groove ran to the QUAY wheel. Water welled from it, carrying flakes of black paint. Mara wiped the plate with her sleeve. More words emerged: KEEP QUAY OPEN UNTIL THE TIDE TURNS.

“But it has turned,” the girl whispered.

“Which tide?” the keeper said.

The first blow struck the stone door. The key rattled but could not turn against the catch.

Mara looked at the harbor master. “When does the tide turn again?”

“At dawn.” His face drained. “Six hours.”

A sharp crack sounded overhead. Dust sifted from the ceiling, followed by a thread of water.

The keeper spoke quickly. “There’s a gauge behind the lighthouse wheel. Tell me where the needle sits.”

Mara reached around the pipe and found a glass dial. Its needle trembled at the edge of a red band.

“Red,” she said.

“Then you have minutes. Turn the lighthouse wheel three revolutions. No more.”

Her father gripped the spokes. On the first turn, a bell sounded far above them. On the second, the water stopped seeping through the ceiling.

On the third, the blows against the door stopped too."
